competences: The learner identifies key facts about bad practices during elections.
The learner explains information about Bad practices before, during and after voting using reference texts.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, spells, reads and writes election malpractices, bad practices, bribery, vote rigging, election.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify facts about bad practices during elections.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer the available sourced questions about Bad practices before, during and after voting.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already studied Uganda and related Social Studies concepts. They build on this earlier work to learn about bad practices during elections.
materials: Chart showing bad practices during elections
Primary Five SST reference on Bad practices before, during and after voting
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the previous SST topic and introduces bad practices during elections. They ask "Mention any three examples of election malpractices." and listen to learners' first responses before referring to the source notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall previously studied content and answer the opening question, explaining their ideas in short sentences.

steps.stage: Development: Meaning and key facts about bad practices during elections
steps.content: Campaigning on the election day Grabbing or stealing the ballot boxes. Bad practice after elections Bribing voters during elections Violence during elections /fighting Torturing of opponents. Making fun of the losers of an election. Mis-recording of election results. A voter who registers more than once Giving wrong information about the voter
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about bad practices during elections on the chalkboard, including "Campaigning on the election day; Grabbing or stealing the ballot boxes. Bad practice after elections". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Features and related facts about bad practices during elections
steps.content: Misdirecting the voters Recording wrong information about voters Making it impossible for voters to vote Unfair splitting of constitutions/ gerrymandering Manipulation of the population make up Blocking candidates from campaigning freely Giving false information about a partner candidate / smear campaign. Intimidating voters viii) Omission of voter names. Creation of ghost polling station.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about bad practices during elections on the chalkboard, including "Misdirecting the voters; Recording wrong information about voters". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Further facts about bad practices during elections
steps.content: Ballot stuffing (putting pre-ticked ballot papers in the ballot box before elections) A candidate refusing to accept defeat. Attacking a voter who has not voted a particular candidate. Unnecessary delay to announce final results. Page 17 Intimidation of voters Grabbing and stealing ballot papers. Campaigning on the voting day. Cheating when counting votes.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about bad practices during elections on the chalkboard, including "Ballot stuffing (putting pre-ticked ballot papers in the ballot box before elections); A candidate refusing to accept defeat.". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.content: Mention any three examples of election malpractices. | Give one example of a universal suf-frage election | What is an open election? | What is an re run as used during election ? | Who was the chairperson of the constituent assembly?
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the original questions, starting with "Mention any three examples of election malpractices." and "Give one example of a universal suf-frage election". They monitor pupils as they answer, check responses against the source material and provide corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the sourced exercise questions independently, consult their copied notes and correct any mistakes after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the factual content on bad practices during elections, asks "Mention any three examples of election malpractices." and follows up with "Give one example of a universal suf-frage election". They confirm the answers and assign the remaining sourced practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners state one important fact from their lesson notes, answer the final oral questions and correct their written work.

assessment: Use the original questions "Mention any three examples of election malpractices." and "Give one example of a universal suf-frage election", along with other listed items, to assess learners' understanding and correct errors from the source material.
homework: Answer the remaining sourced question, including "Which constitution restored Kingdoms in Uganda?"
